why: The one live stability bug, and it costs no attention: the re-soak runs on one board while features are built on the other. Read the card log every day or so; it closes when a soak shows no frame-pace recovery, or one is pinned to its line by the new sub-phases.

The CoCo 3 now runs at full speed in its own build (pizero_coco3), so the open question is how people get it: one firmware that picks the machine (a setting, or which ROM is on the card) or two images. It decides the README, the card layout and every CoCo 3 step after 214. The audio-below-real-time half no longer arises.

CoCo 3 now runs at full speed at 0.89 and 1.79 MHz (PIZERO-213, PIZERO-218), so its feature checks are next: WIDTH 40, palette, GIME timer, HSCREEN modes on hardware. Cheap, and it finds the defects before more work builds on them.

Small, everyday experience win with nothing blocking it: whole-file writes exist, so booting back into the last game is mostly a precedence rule against autorun. A good change of pace between CoCo 3 stages.
Hot-plug: every software path is disproved, but one cheap test is left (unplug and replug through the simple hub). If it works the answer is 'use a hub' and the issue closes.
Other people's screens, which the kits rest on, and it answers whether PIZERO-120's band follows the board or the monitor. Opportunistic: whenever a new screen is to hand.
